messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: embeddings-service error rate spike (P1). 5xxs up from 0.2% -> 9% in last 3m. Canary traffic shows memory OOMs on a subset of hosts. Paging eng-oncall @eng-oncall

eng-oncall: I'm on it. looking at canary cluster now. reported by auto-alerts: embeddings-batcher queue latency increasing. attaching logs in a bit.

Alice Chen: saw the crash loop on canary-agg-03, kernel OOM killer, processes killed: embed-worker. Could be allocator related after latest runtime change.

Raj Patel: which change? recent deploy included the continuous-batching patch + slab allocator tweak (commit 0c4f8b3). That tweak switched default slab size for long sequences.

Maya Thomson: running a quick grep in prod logs — stack shows failure in AllocSlab::grow -> alloc_large() path. Not a tokenizer bug.

Samir Iqbal: DeployBot, what was the rollout percentage and commit id?

DeployBot: Rollout: canary (3% traffic) -> started 2169998600. Commit: 0c4f8b37a (runtime/slab-allocator: adjust slab sizing). Canary hosts: canary-agg-01..04 in us-west-2. No full rollout yet.

Olivia (SE): Customer impact so far? any paid customers hit?

eng-oncall: initial telemetry shows 12 active requests failed in last 5m, errors concentrated on long-context embedding requests (>65k tokens). Top affected: partner-ml-prod (5 failures), search-saas-alpha (3 failures). Not widespread yet but trending up.

Alice Chen: hypothesis: the slab size change increased fragmentation for very large contiguous allocations used by the new batching path. Under heavy long-seq load, processes run out of contiguous address space -> OOM. Repro on staging with long embeddings batches.

Raj Patel: options: 1) kill feature flag to route long-seq requests to legacy allocator (fast rollback), 2) revert the commit (single-commit revert + quick rebuild), 3) apply a one-line hotpatch to restore previous slab threshold. Which is fastest?

Maya Thomson: kill flag should be instant. We have feature flag `runtime.slab_v2` controlled by internal FF service.

Samir Iqbal: I'm going to flip the FF for canary hosts only first, then global if stable. Doing now: `ffctl set runtime.slab_v2 false --scope canary`

eng-oncall: noted. flipping for canary... :gear:

DeployBot: Feature flag change applied to canary group at 2169998702. Confirmed on canary-agg-01/02/03/04.

Alice Chen: monitoring... error rate dropped from 9% -> 1.1% in next minute. Looks like kill worked. :white_check_mark:

Olivia (SE): Great. Do we need to notify customers? CS wants an ETA.

Raj Patel: short-term plan: keep FF disabled globally until we ship hotfix. Medium-term: either revert commit or patch allocator thresholds. Revert simpler but we lose batching perf improvement. Patch is small but needs CI + validation. Which route to take?

Maya Thomson: I prepared a minimal hotpatch that restores old slab threshold for large allocations (3-line change). I can open PR and run quick CI. If tests pass we can push to canary and then rollout.

Samir Iqbal: open the PR and mark it urgent. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1489 (hotfix/slab-alloc-large-restore)

Alice Chen: PR looks good. CI quick-unit passed, integration tests running (approx 7m). I'll watch.

(7m passes)

Alice Chen: integration green. Can we push hotfix to canary as a patch release (single-commit forward)?

Raj Patel: yes. Build artifacts ready. DeployBot, can you do a canary patch deploy with 1 instance at a time?

DeployBot: Starting patch release v2026.3.16-hotfix1 -> canary. Strategy: rolling 1 host at a time over 4 hosts. Command: `deploy --service embeddings --image runtime:v2026.3.16-hotfix1 --canary`

eng-oncall: heads up, we'll watch memory and 5xxs. If any regression, we'll abort.

(rolling deploy in progress)

Alice Chen: patched canary-agg-01: memory stable, no OOM. canary-agg-02 patched: stable. canary-agg-03 is the problematic host — patched now.

Maya Thomson: after patch on canary-agg-03, crash loops stopped. Error rate back to baseline 0.3%.

Samir Iqbal: good. Promote hotfix to global? We should consider a staged rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Given the issue affects only long-context workloads, I'd prefer 25% -> 75% -> 100% to be conservative.

Raj Patel: agreed. Also we need to coordinate CS notifications for the handful of impacted customers. Olivia, can you draft a short proactive note: root cause + mitigation + ETA for full rollout?

Olivia (SE): on it. Draft: "We observed increased 5xx for long-context embeddings after a recent runtime change. We disabled the experimental allocator flag and deployed a hotfix; full rollout expected in ~30 minutes. No data loss. We'll follow up with postmortem." Will ping for approvals.

eng-oncall: starting 25% rollout at 2169998915. Monitor: token processing latency, OOM count, 5xx rate.

DeployBot: 25% -> success -> 75% -> success -> 100% -> success. Full rollout completed at 2169999009.

Alice Chen: confirm metrics: CPU normal, memory map stable, OOMs = 0 since canary patch. Error rate baseline 0.2%.

Raj Patel: closing immediate incident. Action items: - follow-up postmortem with timeline + root cause (Alice/Maya) - consider reverting performance change if patch causes regression in synthetic perf (Raj) - add integration test for long-context batch allocations (Maya) - CS outreach sent (Olivia)
